title: Report of erectile dysfunction after therapy with beta-blockers is related to patient knowledge of side effects and is reversed by placebo
authors: Silvestri A, Galetta P, Cerquetani E, Marazzi G, Patrizi R, Fini M, et al.
population: Men aged 52 plus or minus 7 years with newly diagnosed cardiovascular disease and no erectile dysfunction; authors at the San Raffaele research unit, Rome
funder: not read: the full text requires a subscription and is absent from PubMed Central.
result: All took atenolol 50 mg daily: 32 were blinded to the drug, 32 told the drug but not its side effects, and 32 told the drug and its effects on erectile function. After 3 months erectile dysfunction was reported by 3.1%, 15.6% and 31.2% respectively (P < 0.01). In a crossover phase, sildenafil and placebo were equally effective in reversing erectile dysfunction in all but one of the men reporting it.
